title: EU SEMICeu Core Vocabularies
usedFor: EU public-sector canonical models — conformity (CCCEV), legal entities (Core Business Vocabulary). The natural anchor for operator identity and conformity assertions.
licence: CC-BY 4.0 for the current releases — confirmed 2026-08-11 directly from each vocabulary's own repository (`github.com/SEMICeu/CCCEV`, `github.com/SEMICeu/Core-Business-Vocabulary`), not a survey. Caveat: pre-2.0 CCCEV releases carried the ISA Open Metadata Licence v1.1 instead — re-check the licence of any specific older version/IRI before relying on CC-BY retroactively.
source: https://semiceu.github.io/CCCEV/ (Core Criterion and Core Evidence Vocabulary, v2.1.0, SEMIC Candidate Recommendation 2026-05-12) and https://semiceu.github.io/Core-Business-Vocabulary/ (v2.3.0, released 2026-05-12) — fetched and read directly.
finding: Two distinct vocabularies under this one entry, not one. **CCCEV**'s Criterion/Requirement/Evidence triad is shaped for public-procurement conformity checks — it does not map cleanly onto ESPR's declaration-of-conformity shape (confirmed against CIRPASS-2's own `COMP` module, which models `EUDeclarationOfConformity`/`ConformityCertificate`/`HarmonisedStandard` in ESPR-native terms instead). **Core Business Vocabulary**'s `LegalEntity` (legalName, registeredAddress, activity, companyType) maps much more directly onto an economic-operator/facility identity block. Checked IR (EU) 2026/1778 Art. 12's semantic repository for a textual SEMIC tie — fetched the regulation directly and searched for 'SEMIC', 'Core Vocabularies', 'CCCEV', 'Core Business Vocabulary': zero matches. Art. 11(2)'s permissive language ('may build on existing Union semantic assets') names nothing specific, and no Commission registry page found names SEMIC either. One real but different-layer tie does exist: Art. 12(3) requires the registry's dataset *metadata* to conform to DCAT-AP, itself a SEMIC deliverable — governs metadata-about-datasets, not the DPP attribute semantics layer.
nextStep: Map Core Business Vocabulary's legal-entity terms — or at minimum its property names as a semanticId prefix — for the operator/facility identity block; Commission authorship gives it more regulatory legitimacy than any alternative and the shape fits. CCCEV stays gap-source only: read it for missing evidence-typing concepts, never adopt its IRIs, since its procurement shape doesn't fit ESPR conformity data.
